thread:
maria: Heads up — since the netpolicy rollout at ~08:10 UTC, we've seen KV-sync stalls between slices on us-west2 causing spike in infer latency and a few pod restarts. GPUs themselves look fine.
jason: timeline? which rollout? link?
maria: deploybot posted the policy PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/netpol/merge/4587 — it was the default egress-deny with some ipBlock exceptions. Problem started ~08:12.
ops-bot: deploybot: apply netpol/namespace-default/egress-default-deny by net-eng@08:09 — status: successful
dani: I saw the alerts. tcpdump from one of the affected kv-sync pods shows repeated SYNs with no ACK to 10.244.32.9:11211 then RSTs from sidecar. excerpt:
```
08:15:02.123456 IP 10.244.28.7.53124 > 10.244.32.9.11211: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
08:15:02.223457 IP 10.244.32.9 > 10.244.28.7: RST
```
maria: interestingly the SR-IOV VFs are up and nodetool shows RDMA link still established between nodes but the app-level handshake fails.
net-eng: quick context — the new policy replaced an allow-by-label rule with an ipBlock-based allow list to restrict egress to a set of cluster CIDRs. unintended side-effect was removal of ephemeral port ranges (1024-65535) from allowed ports for intra-cluster services.
jason: so ephemeral ports blocked => existing memcached/kv sync uses high ports for client replies and that gets dropped? but why RST from sidecar?
net-eng: because the service-mesh sidecars (istio) use localhost redirection and sometimes reply from a different source port. combined with CNI (cilium) connection tracking + netpol drop, packets are being rejected at L3 and cilium returns RST to the client. it's a policy shadowing issue.
dani: reproducer: applied the netpol to a test ns with two pods labelled gpu:slice=true and saw identical behavior. kubectl get netpol -n test shows:
```
NAME                   POD-SELECTOR      EGRESS
egress-default-deny    app=backend       to: ipBlock 10.244.0.0/16 ports: tcp:11211
```
maria: but memcached needs ephemeral responses and some control channels over UDP for heartbeat. Not just tcp:11211.
sre-rotation: impact: ~12 pods affected across 4 nodes in us-west2, KV sync latency 95p jumped to 1.8s, no user-facing errors yet but affects throughput. Costly — autoscaler started spinning up extra nodes.
net-eng: immediate mitigation: add an allow rule for pods with label gpu:slice=true to allow TCP+UDP to cluster pod CIDR and ephemeral port range. preparing patch now.
jason: any short-lived workaround? maybe move affected pods to a nodepool with a more permissive network profile?
maria: we can cordon+drain but that takes time and may worsen KV backlog. prefer minimal netpol tweak.
net-eng: patch applied to test namespace at 08:27. rule:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-gpu-eastwest
  namespace: default
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      gpu.slice: "true"
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector: {}
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 1-65535
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 1-65535
```
maria: after applying test patch, kv-sync p50/p95 returned to normal within 2m. memcached logs show no RSTs.
ops-bot: runbook note: created incident ticket NETPOL-2026 and annotated policy PR with mitigation steps.
dani: root cause writeup idea: policy authoring replaced a label-based allowlist with ipBlock-only rules; combined with istio iptables redirect + cilium connection tracking produced RSTs for allowed flows because ephemeral return ports weren't permitted. also SR-IOV/Geneve fragmentation made packet drops less visible in tcpdump.
net-eng: longer term: adding a lint in CI to reject netpols that don't permit ephemeral ports for intra-cluster pod-to-pod connectivity and require a 'gpu:slice' podSelector exemption for known stateful sync workloads. also we'll roll back strict ipBlock rules in non-prod.
sre-rotation: can we add automated perf guard to detect >250ms p95 kv-sync regressions and auto-snooze policy rollouts? would have flagged this before infra autoscaled.
maria: agreed. action items: (1) net-eng to open follow-up PR adding CI lint + policy template (ETA EOD), (2) ops to annotate the rollout runbook, (3) SRE to add perf guard to autoscaler alerting. I'll coordinate.
jason: thanks all. leaving this thread open while we monitor us-west2 nodes.
maria: will post a short postmortem draft after we collect logs.
